title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: one of the rigidity statements of anabelian geometry. Ŷ is a smooth complete curve, Y = Ŷ∖I is hyperbolic, and U ⊂ Y is a dense open with complement Ŷ∖U = J ⊃ I. The neighbouring pages consider two morphisms U → Y. The first is the inclusion i. The second is j, which is shown to differ from i by a translation in the generalized Jacobian. Here α : Y → J'_Y is the Albanese/Abel–Jacobi map into the generalized Jacobian of Ŷ with modulus I, a semi-abelian variety. The relation is α∘j = τ_u∘(α∘i), with u in the kernel of J_Y → J_Ŷ discussed on the previous page. The goal is to show j = i, i.e. u = 0 ('Ouf!' on the next page).

Step 1 (homological equality). Translations in a connected commutative group act trivially on H_1. Also α induces an isomorphism H_1(Y) ≅ H_1(J'_Y) (the abelianized fundamental group of Y equals the Tate module of its Albanese). Together these give H_1(α)H_1(j) = H_1(τ_u)H_1(α)H_1(i) = H_1(α)H_1(i), hence H_1(i) = H_1(j).

Step 2 (combinatorics of cusps). Let f : Ŷ → Ŷ be the extension of j to the completions. Since j(U) ⊂ Y, we have f^{-1}(I) ⊂ J. In H_1(U), the kernel of H_1(U) → H_1(Y) is generated by inertia ('parabolic') subgroups L_x ≅ Ẑ(1), one for each puncture x killed:
- for i, the kernel is generated by the L_x with x ∈ J∖I;
- for j, it is generated by the L_x with x ∈ J∖f^{-1}(I).
The submodule of H_1(U) generated by all L_x (x ∈ J) is Ẑ^J/Ẑ·diagonal, because the sum of the cusp loops vanishes. In this module, two subsets K, K' of J generate the same submodule only if K = K', unless both have cardinality ≥ p−1 (p = card J); any p−1 cusps already generate everything.

Step 3 (next page). Shrinking U, one may assume card(J∖I) > 1. Equality of the kernels then forces f^{-1}(I) = I. So f restricts to an automorphism of Y. Rerunning the argument with Y' = Y ∪ {x} for each x ∈ I shows f fixes I pointwise. In genus 0 (ν ≥ 3) this gives f = id. In genus 1 it gives u = 0 via the earlier Jacobian argument.

The page thus gives an abelian (H_1-level) proof of a separatedness/injectivity statement: a dominant map of hyperbolic curves that is homologically equal to the inclusion and Albanese-translate-equivalent to it is the inclusion. This handles the genus 0 and 1 cases where the naive Abel–Jacobi argument of the previous page failed.
errors: The kernel of H_1(U)→H_1(Y) induced by j should be generated by the L_x with x ∈ J∖f^{-1}(I), not J∖f(I) as written. The punctures killed by j are those not mapping into I. This is a slip; the next page correctly concludes f^{-1}(I)=I.

The subset-comparison statement is stated only roughly: the correct statement is that proper subsets K, K' of J generate equal submodules of Ẑ^J/diag iff K=K' or both have cardinality ≥ p−1. Grothendieck patches this by shrinking U so that card(J∖I)>1.

The claim that H_1(α) is an isomorphism should be read for the abelianized profinite fundamental group, with α the map to the generalized Jacobian of modulus I. This is standard, but implicit on the page.

ideas.what: Translations in the generalized Jacobian act trivially on H_1, so two maps differing by a translation after Abel–Jacobi induce the same map on abelianized π_1.
ideas.modern_name: Albanese property of H_1 for semi-abelian varieties / homotopy invariance under translation

ideas.what: The kernel of H_1(U)→H_1(Y) is generated by the inertia (cusp) subgroups of the filled-in punctures. The cusp subgroups span Ẑ^J/diagonal, which lets one recover which punctures a map kills.
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal inertia / recovery of cusps from abelianized π_1 (weight filtration of H_1 of an open curve)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; group-theoretic recovery of cusps in anabelian geometry: Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki (1990s)

ideas.what: Rigidity: a dominant map U→Y of hyperbolic curves that is π_1/H_1-equivalent to the inclusion is the inclusion, proved by Abel–Jacobi plus cusp combinatorics, with separate treatment of genus 0 and 1.
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of Hom_dom(X,Y) → Hom_out(π_1X,π_1Y) for hyperbolic curves (part of the anabelian Hom conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983, as conjecture); Tamagawa, Mochizuki (proofs of anabelian Hom results)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 formulates the anabelian conjectures; this specific H_1 proof is not known to me in published form

missed.claim: This is an explicit elementary proof, using only abelianized π_1 and generalized Jacobians, of the injectivity/separatedness part of the anabelian Hom statement for open immersions of hyperbolic curves (the setting where a map differs from the inclusion by a translation u). It covers the low-genus cases. The result itself is known and elementary, so this is mostly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck in the Longue Marche period working out such details concretely.
missed.quote: on voit que l'on doit forcément avoir f^{-1}(I) = I i.e. I stable par f
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical documentation of how Grothendieck verified the easy half of anabelian rigidity. It does not add new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine argument (trivial action of translations on H_1, cusp combinatorics in Ẑ^J/diag) proving a known rigidity fact. It is interesting only as a record of Grothendieck's working in the anabelian notes.
transcription_corrections: 'τ_n' should be τ_u (translation by the element u of the previous page): α j = τ_u(α i), H_1(τ_u) = id.
'on fait que tuer les paraboliques' is probably 'on ne fait que tuer les paraboliques' (i.e. kills the cusp/inertia subgroups).
'H_1(U) : H^1(Y)' in the image should read H_1(U) → H_1(Y).
The struck passage reads 'f(U) = Ŷ − f(J) ⊂ Y = Ŷ − I'.
'Or ... αj' likely reads 'Or on a αj = τ_u(αi)'.
The garbled line 'les L_j ... ≃ Ẑ ... Ẑ'' likely refers to the L_j ≅ Ẑ' (prime-to-p or Ẑ(1)) cyclic inertia submodules, whose span in H_1(U) is Ẑ^J/Ẑ (diagonale).
